packages.title: The Drawer of Words That Refuse to Migrate
packages.body: The drawer is full of them. Words that do not travel well. Words that look different in the light of another language. You open it and find the word for nostalgia. It is not a single word. It is a drawer full of little pieces. A scent. A feeling. A shape. The word for it does not exist in English. Not really. The word for it in another language is heavy with meaning. It carries the weight of a place. A time. A person. You try to put it in your pocket. It does not fit. It spills out. It becomes something else. You try to explain it. The words come out wrong. They are flat. They are empty. They are not the word. The word is still in the drawer. It waits. It waits for you to come back with the right words. Or maybe it waits for you to come back with no words at all. Just the feeling. Just the memory. Just the scent. The drawer is full of words that refuse to migrate. They are not lost. They are just waiting. Waiting for the right moment to come out. Waiting for the right person to understand. You know that feeling when you try to describe a color to someone who has never seen it. You try. You fail. The word is not enough. The word is just a key. The real thing is the door it opens. The drawer is full of keys. Keys that do not fit any lock you have. Keys that open doors you did not know existed. You open the drawer. You look at the words. You close the drawer. You leave the words there. You leave them for another day. Another time. Another person. The drawer is full of words that refuse to migrate. They are not lost. They are just waiting. What is a word from your own drawer that you have never been able to translate?
